messages:
morgan (People Ops): Quick Q ":em: employee returned from 12-week sabbatical/parental leave mid-2025 and re-enabled 401(k) deductions on return. During their leave we had a payroll provider cutover. They turned 50 in 2025 so catch-up might apply. Can we remit employer match for (a) pre-leave contributions and (b) contributions withheld after return if the cutover split the contribution records across two vendors? Any docs we need from the employee?
ryan (Payroll): Need dates: leave start, return date, last paycheck before leave, cutover date. Vendors usually accept manual remits for amounts actually withheld; cutover complicates reconciliation but not impossible. Well need signed employee authorization plus payroll export spanning both vendors.
morgan (People Ops): Leave start 2025-03-01, returned 2025-06-22 and elected 401(k) on return. Last pre-leave pay 2025-02-28 (paid), payroll cutover 2025-05-15 (during leave). Employee turned 50 on 2025-04-03.
danielle (Finance): From accounting: employer match is tied to deferrals actually remitted. If deferrals were withheld pre-leave we can remit match. For deferrals after return, if they were withheld under the new vendor we can remit normally. If some withheld contributions ended up in the old vendor records due to cutover, payroll will need to reconcile and instruct which vendor to receive the employer match. We'll need GL code and memo referencing eligible pay periods.
emily (Design): I elected catch-up on return and had some catch-up withheld in July payroll under new vendor. Will that be treated differently?
ryan (Payroll): Catch-up is treated as elective deferral; we can only remit what was actually withheld. So pre-leave withheld amounts and post-return withheld amounts are both eligible. If any amounts are stranded because of cutover mapping issues, we'll work the vendor reconciliation but may need your signed authorization to proceed.
benefits-bot: Policy excerpt: "Employer match is calculated on elective deferrals actually remitted. Catch-up contributions follow IRS rules and require amounts to be withheld on payroll. For cutover-related remittances, submit payroll export + signed authorization to payroll@redwood." <https://docs.redwood.com/benefits/401k-cutover>
morgan (People Ops): Action items: I'll collect the payroll exports (Jan->Feb pre-leave, and Jun->Aug post-return), get Emily's signed authorization for manual remit if needed, and Ryan will open a vendor reconciliation ticket. Danielle  please confirm GL code when I post estimate.
ryan (Payroll): Will open ticket (TKT-401K-CUTOVER-5591) after docs posted. If vendor requires cutoff exception we'll escalate.
danielle (Finance): GL 7021 for employer match. Pre-fund estimate once payroll confirms vendor path.
emily (Design): Thanks 44d will sign the template when you DM it. Appreciate the help!
